key_insight: Language added modest prognostic value to pathology slide features, but prompts did not measurably improve classification and slide-level question answering showed little dependence on images.
clinical_relevance: These findings inform evaluation of pathology AI for cancer prognosis and reporting, not drug discovery or treatment selection.
method: Used released checkpoints and public data in four controlled probes.
Compared slide-only prognosis with added stage-redacted report embeddings.
Tested classification prompts, image removal, and question paraphrasing.
evidence_signal: Across 1,633 TCGA patients, report embeddings increased pooled C-index by 0.019 for progression-free interval and 0.016 for overall survival; SlideChat accuracy was 74.82% with slides versus 74.41% without.
watch_item: Clinical utility remains unestablished, and gains attributed to agentic navigation or few-shot language priors lack sufficient controls to isolate language's contribution.
paper_title: What Language Adds, and at What Cost: Four Controlled Probes of Pathology Vision-Language Models
